result.rule: Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Represent each modeled internal workflow with bpmn:process. Use isExecutable=false unless execution-ready behavior is explicitly required and fully specified.
Create bpmn:collaboration when distinct participants interact and represent every participant as a bpmn:participant pool.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

Follow the BPMN XML schema: never put a documentation element directly inside bpmn:definitions, and never nest a sequenceFlow inside a task, gateway or event. If you add an ioSpecification, it must contain its dataInput and dataOutput elements first, then at least one inputSet and one outputSet, even if empty: <bpmn:inputSet/><bpmn:outputSet/>.

args.text: When a process description states the outcome that concludes a process, label the end event to reflect that stated outcome, rather than a contradictory outcome.

trace.reason: Check whether documented guidance already covers faithful end-event labels or would forbid this instruction.

result.rule: Use end events for terminal outcomes. An end event has no outgoing sequence flow and is not the target of a message flow.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.

Respect event positions: a none intermediate event is catch-only in normal flow and never on a boundary; link events are intermediate-only, thrown and caught in pairs at the same process level, and a catching link has no incoming sequence flow; terminate is an end event only.
Distinguish message tasks from message events: a task models performed work; an event models a message occurrence affecting flow.

args.text: When the description states a terminal outcome, label the end event to reflect that outcome and do not label it with a contradictory outcome.

result.rule: When the description identifies a condition for taking a branch but does not say that the alternative ends the process: Label an end event only with an outcome explicitly stated as the process outcome; otherwise use a neutral end-event label.

When the description explicitly states the outcome that marks the process as complete: label the end event with a concise phrase that faithfully names that outcome, rather than a generic label or an unnecessarily detailed restatement

When the description identifies alternative terminal outcomes and states an action associated with at least one outcome: Model each outcome on its own branch, representing any stated action that realizes an outcome as a task before a terminal end event.

When the description distinguishes an action that occurs before a later recording, confirmation, or other outcome: Model that action as a distinct activity in the sequence; do not omit it or use a terminal outcome event as its substitute.
